author: First State Times
title: Lacrosse teams advance and tennis champions announced in DIAA state tournaments
text:
The Delaware Interscholastic Athletic Association announced on May 20 that several boys and girls lacrosse teams have advanced in the ongoing DIAA State Tournament, with updated results from recent matches. The organization also confirmed the conclusion of the 2026 Boys and Girls Tennis State Championships, naming individual and doubles champions.
The announcement matters to local sports communities as it highlights both tournament progress for lacrosse and recognizes top performers in high school tennis. These updates inform fans, athletes, coaches, and families about key outcomes and upcoming events within Delaware’s high school athletic scene.
In girls lacrosse Round 2 play, Sussex Academy defeated Padua with a score of 19-12 while St. Andrew’s won against Smyrna by a margin of 14-3. Additional girls’ matchups are scheduled to finalize the quarterfinal field. On the boys’ side, Smyrna bested Milford 14-6, Newark Charter overcame Polytech 13-9, while weather delays affected other games including Wilmington Friends versus Sussex Academy—set to resume tomorrow—and Archmere against Indian River now rescheduled for tomorrow evening.
For suspended boys’ lacrosse games due to weather interruptions—specifically Wilmington Friends vs Sussex Academy and Archmere vs Indian River—the association stated that admission will not be charged when these contests resume. Fans who attended previously do not need new tickets; however, refunds will not be issued.
In tennis competition concluded earlier this week, Caroline Jiao (Archmere) claimed the Girls’ First Singles title along with her teammates Akilah Yu (Second Singles), Susie Shipley (Third Singles), Lauren Nguyen & Jessica Li (First Doubles), and Emily Shipley & Rebecca Wang (Second Doubles). For boys’, Ryan He (Charter) took First Singles honors alongside Renzo Gopez (Second Singles), Johannes Chow (Third Singles), Lucas Sturges & Charles McLellan from St. Andrew’s winning First Doubles, and Jack Marshall & John Gavenonis from Tower Hill securing Second Doubles.
Tickets for all remaining state tournament games can be purchased online via GoFan. Semifinal and championship matches will be streamed live on the NFHS Network so fans can follow remotely through links provided on the DIAA website or social media platforms.
